about.title: Hillsborough Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Hillsborough is a quiet, low-density community tucked into San Mateo County, but that doesn't mean residents are immune from defective consumer goods, faulty vehicle parts, malfunctioning appliances, or unsafe household equipment. When a product fails and someone gets hurt, California law often allows the injured person to pursue a strict liability claim — meaning you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. This can apply to a poorly designed item, a manufacturing error, or a failure to warn about a known risk. Whether the product was purchased locally or online and shipped to a Hillsborough address, multiple parties in the supply chain — the maker, distributor, or retailer — may share responsibility. We are a free service that connects injured Hillsborough residents with our team, who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, without any pressure or fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Us About a Defective Product

items.title: Strict Liability May Apply
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to prove negligence — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. We can help identify whether the defect was in design, manufacturing, or warning labels.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all share liability for a defective product. Our team can help determine who was involved in getting that product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any receipts can be critical evidence. We can advise you on how to protect that proof before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California often applies strict liability to defective products, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that anyone was negligent. We can review your situation and explain which theory may fit your case.

items.question: I live in Hillsborough but bought the product elsewhere — does that matter?
items.answer: Usually not. What matters more is where you were injured and where you live, both of which are relevant to a San Mateo County claim. We can look at the details of your purchase and injury to figure out the right approach.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try not to throw it away, alter it, or attempt repairs. Keeping the item, along with packaging, manuals, and receipts, helps preserve evidence that may support your claim. We can advise on proper storage and next steps.

items.question: Is there a cost to contact us about your product liability claim?
items.answer: No. There's no upfront cost, and there's no obligation to move forward. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
